title: Reading scales
log: 2026-11-01T08:04:34Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: Neither bank point teaches reading measuring instruments to the nearest marked unit; the scale drawings point is about plan ratios and the geography point is about the spatial scale of an issue, so neither is the same idea.

draft.title: Reading scales
card: First find what each small mark is worth. Pick two marked numbers next to each other, find the gap between them, then divide by the number of spaces.
Read the scale at the mark the pointer or liquid is closest to. Give the answer to the nearest marked unit.
For a jug, read at eye level, at the flat top of the liquid. Always include the unit, such as mL, °C or kg.
The marks 0 and 100 mL have 5 spaces between them. Each space is 100 ÷ 5 = 20 mL. The third mark after 0 reads 60 mL.
draft.remember: Work out what each small mark is worth before you read the value.

a.q: On a jug, the marks 200 mL and 300 mL have 4 equal spaces between them. What does each small mark count for?
a.why: The gap is 300 − 200 = 100 mL, shared over 4 spaces: 100 ÷ 4 = 25 mL. Using 20 mL would mean dividing by 5, which is the number of marks, not the number of spaces.
a.clue: Divide the gap between the numbers by the number of spaces.

b.q: A thermometer is marked every 2 °C. The 20 °C mark is labelled, and the liquid ends one small mark above 20 °C. What is the reading?
b.why: Each small mark is worth 2 °C, so one mark above 20 °C is 22 °C. Reading 21 °C treats each mark as 1 °C, which the scale does not show.
b.clue: What is each small mark worth on this scale?
